In the "Action Plan," we set ambitious targets, requiring all banks to commit to achieving net-zero emissions in their own operations by 2030 or earlier, and net-zero emissions in their financing by 2050 or earlier. We also require all banks to enhance the disclosure of climate-related risks and opportunities. While continuously strengthening the climate risk management of banks, we also provide guidance for the transition planning of banks to help them enhance their transition capabilities and better manage related risks. We are also conducting preparatory work with relevant stakeholders to align Hong Kong's sustainable disclosure requirements with international standards, aiming to further improve the industry's transparency in related activities. Additionally, we are optimizing the Hong Kong Sustainable Finance Taxonomy launched last May to include more sustainable activities (including transition activities). We hope to guide more capital toward sustainable and transition-related projects by providing clear guidelines. Climate change brings significant physical and transition risks, which may affect the long-term financial performance and value of the Exchange Fund's investment projects. At the same time, however, it also brings opportunities for the Exchange Fund to achieve growth and drive positive impacts. Our experience proves that investment returns and positive sustainable impacts can be coordinated and do not conflict. In view of this, we are committed to achieving net-zero emissions for the Exchange Fund's "investment portfolio" by 2050 or earlier, and have committed in the "Action Plan" to support Asia's climate transition through the Exchange Fund's investments. Currently, the proportion of sustainable investments in the "investment portfolio" has already exceeded ten percent. To further promote sustainable investment in the region, the HKMA established strategic partnerships with the Asian Development Bank, the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank, and the International Finance Corporation in November last year to accelerate the low-carbon economic transition in Asia through joint investments. Additionally, we published the first "HKMA ESG Expectations" document in September last year to further encourage fund managers to actively exercise ownership rights and adopt good sustainable investment practices. The flow of capital is particularly crucial for accelerating the region's transition. As an international financial hub and the preferred location for arranging international sustainable bond issuances for issuers in Asia (including provincial and municipal governments in the Mainland), Hong Kong plays a vital role in guiding capital to accelerate the region's transition. The "Action Plan" outlines the vision of developing Hong Kong into the region's premier sustainable finance platform and the goal of promoting sustainable finance innovation. From leveraging the exemplary role of the "Government Green Bond Programme" to drive green bond innovation (including the issuance of the world's first multi-currency digital bonds in February last year), to expanding the scope of the "Green and Sustainable Finance Funding Scheme" to include transition finance instruments in May last year, and the launch of the "Digital Bond Funding Scheme" in November last year, we have remained committed to encouraging regional issuers to utilize Hong Kong's financial platform to raise the funds needed for decarbonization transition. To achieve a robust transition, a supportive, inclusive, and accessible sustainable development ecosystem is required in addition to capital and innovation. This includes reliable sustainable development data, high-transparency information disclosure, and industry professionals with relevant knowledge and skills. To this end, we committed in the "Action Plan" to support the promotion of high-quality and comprehensive sustainable disclosure, and to strive to fill the gap in sustainable finance talent and knowledge in the region. We have made good progress in assisting relevant stakeholders and facilitating sustainable disclosure, particularly by providing convenient and easy-to-use climate disclosure templates to facilitate sustainable disclosure for SMEs. We also launched a "Green and Sustainable Finance" professional module under the Banking Professional Qualifications framework in November last year to enhance the relevant knowledge and skills of local banking staff. Furthermore, through the inaugural Hong Kong Green Week held in February last year and other events, we have engaged people from all walks of life in discussions on sustainable development, thereby promoting cooperation and innovation. Internally, the HKMA is committed to ensuring that our operations align with the vision of sustainable development. We committed in the "Action Plan" to achieve net-zero emissions in our own operations by 2030 or earlier, which is 20 years ahead of our original commitment. Additionally, we are actively preparing to meet international sustainable disclosure standards in accordance with the roadmap issued by the Government. We began adopting electric vehicles in 2024 and have incorporated low-carbon emissions as a screening factor in the procurement process. At the same time, we continue to improve work efficiency through digitalization, foster a culture of sustainable development within the institution, and encourage employees to actively participate in sustainable development work. Multilateral cooperation has always been the cornerstone of the global response to climate change, but the reshaping of the international landscape and drastic changes in geopolitical situations have added variables to global climate action. However, climate change is an undeniable fact and is gradually intensifying. In our work to address climate change, the current situation does not allow us to slacken in the slightest. We firmly believe that promoting an orderly and inclusive transition will help mitigate the impact of climate risks on Hong Kong's financial system and bring opportunities in the process. Stepping into 2025, we will continue to forge ahead, strive to advance sustainable development work, and deepen relationships with like-minded partners. Despite the severe challenges, we will remain committed as always to supporting the construction of a sustainable future for Hong Kong, Asia, and other regions.

Climate change represents a major challenge for our generation. As an international financial centre and a sustainable finance hub in Asia, Hong Kong strives to play a pioneering role in supporting sustainable development both in Asia and globally. In October 2024, the HKMA released its “Sustainable Finance Action Plan” (the “Action Plan”), outlining its vision in this area, including future directions, timelines for achieving various objectives, and expectations for collaboration with the industry to advance related efforts. The HKMA intends to strengthen Hong Kong’s financial sector and its own capacity to address climate-related risks by formulating strategic policies, enhancing regulatory coordination, and improving internal operations, thereby facilitating Asia’s transition towards a more sustainable economy. Through active participation in international and regional discussions, the HKMA also aims to exert influence in shaping green and sustainable finance policies and standards at both regional and global levels. As a banking regulator, the HKMA focuses on enhancing the climate resilience of banks and ensuring their stability as they transition to net-zero emissions. Our key priorities in 2025 include:   – Conducting a new round of thematic reviews on banks’ climate risk management practices, along with a third round of consultation meetings, to assess banks’ compliance with relevant HKMA regulatory requirements and further improve their climate risk management capabilities;   – Refining efforts to integrate climate risk stress testing into the HKMA’s regulatory-led stress testing framework;   – Continuing to incorporate climate considerations into the HKMA’s regulatory review processes;   – Initiating preparatory work on formulating regulatory requirements for local banks to implement the upcoming Basel Committee on Banking Supervision’s third pillar disclosure framework on climate-related financial risks, as well as the International Sustainability Standards Board’s (ISSB) standards;   – Finalising the drafting of a new section, GS-2, in the “Regulatory Policy Manual” to provide guidance to banks on transition planning; and   – Sharing with the industry best practices in climate risk management and the application of green fintech solutions.    Beyond its role as a banking regulator, the HKMA also acts as a facilitator, striving to nurture the development of a green and sustainable finance ecosystem and supporting banks in financing the transition process. We published the first phase of the “Hong Kong Taxonomy for Sustainable Finance”, which serves as a tool for industry stakeholders to identify green and sustainable economic activities and facilitates corresponding financing. The HKMA has now commenced work on the second phase of the taxonomy, aiming to expand its scope by incorporating transition-related elements, additional green economic activities, and climate adaptation objectives. Furthermore, building on the success of the third FiNETech event in 2024 and the Green Fintech Challenge in 2023, we will host another Green Fintech event in 2025 to encourage banks to adopt green fintech solutions.    Hong Kong is well-positioned to meet regional demand for sustainable financing. To reinforce this role, we will continue to assist the Government in implementing the “Government Sustainable Bond Programme”, whose expanded scope will now include sustainable projects such as those with social impact objectives. This move will further develop Hong Kong’s local green and sustainable bond market and serve as a model for other potential issuers in the region. Additionally, we will continue to provide financial support via the “Green and Sustainable Finance Grant Scheme” to encourage more regional borrowers to raise sustainable funds through Hong Kong’s financing platforms. We will also intensify promotional efforts to attract more mainland and overseas governments, institutions, and enterprises to raise green funds in Hong Kong. Concurrently, we will continue to catalyse and support sustainable financial innovation, including through the “Digital Bond Grant Scheme” which provides financial assistance to prospective issuers of digital green bonds. Although market demand for high-quality sustainability disclosures from institutions and enterprises continues to rise, the capabilities and readiness levels of different entities in this regard vary, with some requiring additional guidance and support. In light of this, the HKMA will continue to collaborate with other members of the Inter-Agency Steering Group on Green and Sustainable Finance to make sustainability disclosures more accessible and inclusive. For instance, we will continue to provide banks and their clients with a wider range of tools related to climate disclosure, including user-friendly templates and supporting resources for sustainability reporting; explore how technology can further enhance the usability of existing resources; and partner with major local industry associations to deliver relevant training programmes. Given the rapidly evolving nature of the sustainable finance market, there is a pressing need to expand the local talent pool and bridge knowledge gaps both in Hong Kong and across the region. In 2025, a key priority for the HKMA will be working with the banking sector to develop professional-level training courses under the “Green and Sustainable Finance” module within the “Banking Professional Qualifications Framework”. Additionally, through the upcoming “Future Banking Talent 2026–2030” study, we aim to identify areas where further industry training is needed. We also plan to collaborate with key stakeholders to promote the government-funded “Pilot Scheme on Green and Sustainable Finance Training” and review its scope of application. At the regional level, the HKMA will continue to partner with the International Finance Corporation via the Green Commercial Banking Alliance to launch targeted initiatives in Asia, such as conducting research on green finance, providing unique market analyses, offering targeted skills development and training support, fostering community engagement, facilitating potential green investment opportunities, and providing practical guidance to help banks incorporate green finance into their core business strategies. As a responsible investor, the HKMA is committed to achieving net-zero emissions across its Exchange Fund portfolio by 2050, thereby supporting the broader economic transition. We will continue to enhance the sustainability of the Exchange Fund’s investments through pragmatic and rigorous responsible investment practices, with a primary focus on the long-term resilience of our asset portfolio while also exploring investment opportunities that yield positive climate outcomes. The HKMA strives to set an example in corporate sustainability. In line with the timeline outlined in the “Action Plan” for accelerating progress towards net-zero targets, we will progressively integrate environmental and social considerations into our strategies, risk assessments, and reporting processes, further advancing our corporate sustainability efforts. Specifically, in 2025 we will conduct a dual materiality assessment to gain deeper insights into the potential financial and non-financial impacts of climate change and other sustainability issues, ensuring that we focus on matters of greatest significance. Furthermore, we will carry out energy audits and utilise technological solutions to evaluate the material impact of climate risks on our offices and operations, thereby strengthening our climate resilience and risk preparedness. We fully support the Hong Kong Sustainable Disclosure Roadmap released by the Government and are actively preparing to implement sustainability disclosures in accordance with ISSB standards. In 2025, the HKMA will continue to uphold its commitment to energy efficiency and conservation by selecting data centres for planned upgrades based on these principles. We will also expand digital initiatives aimed at promoting sustainability and operational efficiency, including developing digital tools and platforms to facilitate paperless processes and waste reduction, thereby enhancing the overall digital experience for our staff, banks, and the general public.

Climate change affects every aspect of human life, and everyone can contribute to mitigating its impacts. Leveraging its multiple roles as a central bank, banking regulator, market facilitator, responsible investor, and sustainability advocate, the HKMA plays a part in promoting and accelerating the transition to net-zero emissions in Hong Kong and across Asia. The HKMA has established a robust governance framework for sustainability that guides the development of relevant strategies and policies, oversees implementation efforts, and ensures that sustainability considerations are integrated into its own operations. Committed to sound corporate governance, the HKMA has put in place a well-structured governance framework for sustainability featuring clear accountability mechanisms and high transparency. This framework ensures that sustainability factors are effectively incorporated into the HKMA’s strategic planning and decision-making processes, while also providing effective mechanisms to monitor and evaluate progress and outcomes in sustainability initiatives. The HKMA’s sustainability governance framework comprises the following components:   – The Exchange Fund Advisory Committee and its relevant subcommittees, which oversee the HKMA’s work, including its sustainability efforts, and provide recommendations;   – The Green and Sustainable Development Steering Committee (the Steering Committee), chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, which provides leadership at the management level regarding the HKMA’s overall environmental, social, and governance (ESG) strategies and policies;   – In the realm of responsible investment, the ESG Committee under the Exchange Fund Investment Office coordinates and oversees all ESG-related activities within the Office; and   – For other functional areas, various teams and working groups are responsible for planning and implementing sustainability measures related to banking and market development as well as the HKMA’s own operations. At the cross-sectoral level, the HKMA and the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) jointly established the Inter-Agency Steering Group on Green and Sustainable Finance (the Steering Group) to coordinate efforts among financial regulators, government departments, industry stakeholders, and other parties, thereby accelerating the development of green and sustainable finance in Hong Kong. Given the significant expansion of the HKMA’s sustainability initiatives over recent years, the Steering Committee was established in October 2023 as a central platform to lead and better coordinate all sustainability efforts across the HKMA’s various functional areas. Its responsibilities include:   – Providing guidance on the formulation of strategies, policies, and plans related to ESG matters in four key areas: banking, development of the green and sustainable finance ecosystem, Exchange Fund investments, and internal operations;   – Overseeing implementation of ESG-related plans by various HKMA departments;   – Evaluating the HKMA’s performance and achievements in attaining its ESG objectives; and   – Supervising external communication strategies. The Steering Committee is chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, with three Deputy Chief Executives serving as permanent members. Additionally, Assistant Chief Executives responsible for key functions related to green and sustainable development are invited to attend Steering Committee meetings to report on major achievements and future plans. The Steering Committee meets regularly, with support provided by relevant working groups under the Banking Department, Institutional Development and Operations Department, External Relations Department, and the Exchange Fund Investment Office. Apart from developing and implementing its own sustainability measures, the HKMA and the SFC jointly launched the Steering Group in May 2020. Acting as a cross-institutional platform, the Steering Group provides strategic direction and coordinates cross-sectoral efforts within the financial industry to address climate and environmental risks, thereby reinforcing Hong Kong’s position as a leading green and sustainable finance hub in Asia and globally. For further details on the Steering Group’s work, please refer to the chapter “Strengthening the Development of a Green and Sustainable Finance Ecosystem.”

Climate change can pose risks to the financial system. The HKMA has been committed to strengthening the ability of Hong Kong's financial system to cope with climate risks, while contributing to Hong Kong's climate goals and the global sustainability agenda. Banks face impacts from various sustainability and climate-related matters in their daily business operations and must therefore proactively manage climate risks. At the same time, banks play an important role in the financial system by directing funds toward green and sustainable projects. As the banking regulator, the HKMA places special emphasis on building the capacity of banks to respond to and manage climate risks, and accelerating the efforts of banks to support the transition to a low-carbon economic model. In October, the HKMA published the "Sustainable Finance Action Plan" (the "Action Plan"), outlining the HKMA's vision to further consolidate Hong Kong's position as a regional sustainable finance centre and support sustainability in Asia and globally. The "Action Plan" includes eight targets across four areas. To assist the industry in achieving the targets of the relevant banking policies, we have been carrying out the following work. All banks are committed to achieving net-zero emissions in their own operations by 2030 or earlier, and to achieving net-zero financed emissions by 2050 or earlier. All banks have increased transparency regarding climate-related risks and opportunities. In December, the HKMA shared best practices for transition planning with the industry and launched industry consultations on the draft of Unit GS-2 "Transition Planning" of the "Regulatory Policy Manual". The new unit aims to provide guidance on enhancing the capacity of banks to cope with the net-zero transition and related risk management. Furthermore, we are reviewing the supervisory review process used to assess and monitor the capital adequacy levels of banks and determine their Pillar capital requirements, with the aim of incorporating factors proposed by the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (BCBS) regarding the effective management of climate-related financial risks into the assessment process, and encouraging banks to strengthen their risk management frameworks (including transition planning) to cope with climate risks. The HKMA has been committed to aligning local sustainability disclosure requirements with international standards, including the International Sustainability Standards Board (ISSB) standards and the BCBS's disclosure framework for climate-related financial risks. Specifically, the HKMA is analyzing the latest developments in sustainability disclosure and supporting the Hong Kong Institute of Certified Public Accountants in conducting a technical feasibility study on the adoption of ISSB standards. Promoting green and transition finance is key to implementing the "Action Plan". In May, the HKMA published the Hong Kong Sustainable Finance Taxonomy (the "Taxonomy") to address industry concerns over greenwashing and to help guide the flow of funds toward green and sustainable activities. The Taxonomy covers 12 economic activities under four industries, aiming to align with common green taxonomies as well as the taxonomies of Mainland China and the EU, while also incorporating relevant elements to respond to local circumstances. We have commenced the second phase of work to expand the scope covered by the Taxonomy and are consulting a wide range of stakeholders to further facilitate the flow of green and sustainable funds. During the year, the HKMA further strengthened the supervision of climate risk management in banks and was committed to supporting banks in building the capacity to manage climate-related risks and opportunities and to cope with climate change. The HKMA has also completed all work to incorporate climate risks into the banking supervisory procedures as set out in the two-year plan formulated in 2022. To enhance the ability of banks to manage climate risks, the HKMA shared best practices observed during thematic reviews and consultation meetings with the banking industry, primarily including: - establishing a robust governance framework with clearly defined responsibilities for the Board of Directors and senior management; - ensuring effective oversight of key areas of climate-related risk matters (1) promoting and overseeing the effective formulation and execution of climate strategies; (2) exercising appropriate oversight of climate-related risk management; and (3) establishing a sound climate risk culture within the institution. The HKMA held a Balanced Supervision Roundtable on climate risk management in August. At the roundtable, bank representatives and HKMA participants exchanged views on various climate risk-related issues, including the challenges faced by banks in climate risk management, climate risk stress testing, transition planning, and finance, among others. This roundtable provided an interactive platform for information sharing and assisted the HKMA in its work on climate risk supervision and other related aspects. The HKMA conducted a round of thematic reviews on the climate risk management frameworks and practices of banks, assessing their robustness and adequacy based on the regulatory expectations set out in Unit GS-1 "Climate Risk Management" of the Regulatory Policy Manual. The thematic reviews covered the entire risk management process, including risk identification, measurement, oversight, reporting, control and mitigation, as well as climate risk scenario analysis and stress testing. The HKMA held the second series of consultation meetings to assess the progress of a new batch of banks in implementing Unit GS-1 "Climate Risk Management" of the Regulatory Policy Manual and to understand the challenges they face. The consultation meetings also covered the latest regulatory and market developments in climate-related areas, including transition planning, disclosure frameworks and standards, and greenwashing issues. We provided feedback and guidance based on the specific circumstances of the banks to support their work in climate risk management. The HKMA completed the second round of Climate Risk Stress Testing (CRST) for the banking industry in 2024, with 21 retail banks and the Hong Kong branches of 25 international banking groups participating. The results showed that under various scenarios (including those assuming the simultaneous occurrence of climate risks and macroeconomic downturns), the Hong Kong banking industry continued to demonstrate strong resilience against severe climate-related shocks. Compared with the CRST pilot program, participating banks significantly improved their capabilities in measuring and assessing climate risks. The report describing the CRST results and the best practices observed by the HKMA during the process was published in February 2025. The HKMA understands that banks face numerous challenges regarding data and methodologies in climate risk management; therefore, it has been committed to various initiatives to promote the application of technology to address these challenges. To address the lack of physical risk-related data and analytical tools for climate risk assessment, the HKMA launched a physical risk assessment platform in May, enabling banks to assess the potential impact of physical risks on residential and commercial buildings in Hong Kong under different climate scenarios. Looking ahead, the HKMA will enhance the platform by incorporating more local data and responding to user feedback. Additionally, the HKMA is collaborating with relevant stakeholders to promote the adoption of green fintech solutions by banks and the overall financial services industry. During the year, we released practical application guidelines and two "RegTech Use Case Briefings" (English version) outlining technology solutions for environmental, social and governance (ESG) and sustainability assessments, as well as greenwashing risk management. We also held the third "FiNETech," bringing together over 150 financial institutions and technology companies to explore cooperation in green fintech. The HKMA fully understands that climate change may pose potential risks to the financial system and has therefore incorporated a broader range of climate factors and scenarios into financial risk analysis and research to strengthen current oversight work. The HKMA takes climate change into account in its ongoing monitoring of financial stability risks and incorporates analyses of climate-related risks into its various financial stability reports. Through active participation in the scenario design and analysis working group under the Network for Greening the Financial System (NGFS), the HKMA assists in further enriching climate scenarios, helping central banks and supervisors understand the impacts of climate change on the macroeconomy and finance. In November, the NGFS published the fifth edition of the Long-term Climate Macro-Financial Scenarios to provide a reference for forward-looking climate risk assessments. As a member of the Transition Planning Working Group under the Financial Stability Board, the HKMA participates in analyzing the interactions between the transition planning of financial and non-financial corporations and financial stability, enabling policymakers to examine climate-related financial risks from a forward-looking and dynamic perspective. The HKMA published the "Practice Guidelines on the Application of Green Technology by Banks" (English version) to provide financial institutions with best practices for utilizing green technology to promote their net-zero transition. In terms of research, the HKMA conducts several applied research projects to explore the impacts of climate change on the financial industry and the overall economy. Research topics include the cross-border transmission of climate transition risks, the role of corporate environmental performance in resisting monetary policy shocks, the impact of climate-related factors on foreign direct investment flows, and the role of the financial industry in moving towards a low-carbon economy. The aforementioned research findings not only enhance our understanding of how climate change affects financial stability but also provide valuable insights into the green and sustainable finance ecosystem, aiding in the formulation of relevant policies. Locally, these studies help strengthen the HKMA's ongoing monitoring and assessment of the impacts of climate change on financial stability. Research findings are also shared with a wide range of stakeholders through various channels, such as international forums and the *HKMA Research Memorandum*. The Hong Kong Monetary and Financial Research Centre (Research Centre) under the Academy of Finance published a research paper on the impact of carbon pricing on corporate performance. The study provides evidence showing that low-emission enterprises can derive significant benefits from carbon pricing and highlights its role in improving efficiency by reallocating resources from high-emission to low-emission enterprises. The study is featured in the Research Centre's *Insights from Monetary Research* and is shared with local and international scholars and policy researchers. The HKMA's "Liquidity Facilities" is a collateralized liquidity arrangement that provides timely liquidity support to banks in need. The HKMA has incorporated sustainability considerations when assessing eligible collateral under this framework. The HKMA actively participates in international and regional discussions on addressing climate risks and promoting sustainable finance as mainstream. Through participation in these areas, we help facilitate international and regional policy dialogues on addressing climate change and its impacts on financial stability, and draw insights from these to help strengthen the climate resilience of Hong Kong's financial system.

To strengthen Hong Kong’s position as a leading regional hub for green and sustainable finance, the HKMA is committed to raising market awareness and participation, providing necessary infrastructure and incentives, and supporting relevant international initiatives to align with global standards. As outlined in the HKMA’s “Sustainable Finance Action Plan,” the HKMA strives to enhance the green and sustainable finance ecosystem by promoting net-zero financing and fostering more inclusive sustainable development. Specifically, we aim to position Hong Kong as the preferred sustainable financing platform for borrowers both regionally and globally, support technological innovation in the green financial sector, improve sustainable disclosure practices within the industry, expand the local pool of green talent, and address knowledge gaps related to sustainable finance in Hong Kong and the region. Positioning Hong Kong as the preferred sustainable financing platform regionally and globally; fostering innovation in sustainable finance; promoting high-quality and comprehensive sustainable disclosure; and bridging talent and knowledge gaps in sustainable finance within the region. To demonstrate the government’s commitment to tackling climate change, promoting green finance, and developing Hong Kong into a more sustainable and livable city, the “Government Green Bond Programme” was launched in 2018. To date, the HKMA has assisted the government in issuing green bonds worth approximately USD 280 billion in total, which were sold to institutional and retail investors. The proceeds have been allocated to over 110 government green projects, including green building, waste management and recycling, energy efficiency, and energy conservation. With each issuance, we continue to innovate and expand the features of green bonds—including currency options, tenors, and distribution channels—thereby setting a precedent for other public and private green bond issuers in the region. In 2024, to amplify the programme’s impact and further consolidate Hong Kong’s status as a green and sustainable finance hub, its scope was broadened to include sustainable projects and it was renamed the “Government Sustainable Bond Programme.”  To enhance transparency and accountability under the Sustainable Bond Programme, the government publishes an annual “Green Bond Report” detailing how funds raised through green bonds are allocated and their anticipated environmental benefits. In July, the HKMA assisted the government in issuing institutional green bonds worth approximately USD 30 billion under the Sustainable Bond Programme. This multi-currency issuance featured bonds denominated in RMB, USD, and EUR with varying tenors. The bonds attracted participation from diverse investor groups, receiving strong demand with total subscriptions exceeding USD 150 billion. Notably, the 20-year and 30-year RMB green bonds marked the government’s first-ever issuances of such tenors, establishing new benchmarks in the market and further underscoring the exemplary role of the Sustainable Bond Programme. These bonds also enriched the range of offshore RMB investment products available in Hong Kong. Moreover, the enthusiastic response from global investors reflects their confidence in Hong Kong’s efforts to advance green and sustainable development. To encourage more regional borrowers to leverage Hong Kong’s financing platform for sustainable development funding, the HKMA continues to administer the “Green and Sustainable Finance Subsidy Scheme” introduced in May 2021, which provides subsidies for eligible green and sustainable debt instruments issued in Hong Kong. The scheme has been well received by the industry; as of end-2024, it has approved subsidies for some 500 green and sustainable debt instruments issued in Hong Kong, totaling over USD 1,400 billion. In May 2024, the scheme was extended for three more years until 2027, with its scope expanded to include transition bonds and loans. This extension and expansion aim to motivate borrowers in relevant industries across the region to utilize Hong Kong’s transition financing platform for gradual decarbonization. – Subsidies approved for some 500 green and sustainable debt instruments issued in Hong Kong, totaling over USD 1400 billion (as of end-2024);   – Scheme extended to 2027 with expanded coverage to transition financing instruments. Meanwhile, the HKMA has been actively promoting Hong Kong’s sustainable financing platform, achieving commendable results. In August, the Shenzhen Municipal People’s Government conducted its fourth offshore issuance of local government bonds in Hong Kong, totaling RMB 70 billion, which included RMB 27 billion in green bonds, RMB 10 billion in sustainable bonds, and RMB 9 billion in social responsibility bonds. In September, the Guangdong Provincial People’s Government made its debut offshore bond issuance in Hong Kong, raising RMB 50 billion, of which RMB 15 billion comprised green bonds. In October, the People’s Government of Hainan Province conducted its third offshore bond issuance in Hong Kong, totaling RMB 30 billion, which included RMB 10 billion in blue bonds and RMB 10 billion in sustainable bonds. These bond issuances once again highlight Hong Kong’s unique role in facilitating the flow of green and sustainable financing between the Chinese mainland and the rest of the world. Thanks to these efforts, Hong Kong continues to solidify its standing as the preferred platform for sustainable finance in Asia. According to statistics released by the International Capital Market Association, Hong Kong remained the largest hub in Asia for arranging international green and sustainable bond issuances in 2024, with a total volume of USD 431 billion arranged through Hong Kong, accounting for 45% of the regional total. To spur innovation in sustainable finance, the HKMA assisted the government in issuing two landmark tokenized green bonds in 2023 and 2024—the world’s first tokenized government green bonds and the first multi-currency digital bonds, respectively. These issuances reflect the government’s support for market participants in applying asset tokenization and innovative technologies to green and sustainable finance. In November, the HKMA launched the “Digital Bond Subsidy Scheme” to encourage and support innovation within Hong Kong’s green and sustainable finance markets by promoting the issuance of digital bonds, including digital green bonds. A working group on sustainable disclosure under the Inter-Agency Steering Group on Green and Sustainable Finance has been working to facilitate Hong Kong’s adoption of the International Sustainability Standards Board’s (ISSB) standards. In December 2024, the government released the “Hong Kong Sustainable Disclosure Roadmap,” outlining a clear pathway for large listed companies to fully adopt ISSB standards by 2028 at the latest. The HKMA has been collaborating closely with local and international partners to help entities at various stages of readiness achieve high-quality sustainable disclosure, thereby making such practices more accessible and inclusive. Notably, we continue to encourage the use of the “Climate and Environmental Risk Questionnaire for Non-Listed Companies,” jointly developed by the Steering Group and CDP in 2022. This questionnaire provides an easy-to-use disclosure template, facilitating sustainable disclosure efforts by enterprises, including small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). An electronic version of the questionnaire was launched in February 2024, allowing companies to submit responses online (see the QR code below). Based on industry feedback and recent international developments, the HKMA is refining the questionnaire to make it even more user-friendly; measures include identifying core questions and providing common use cases. We are also striving to improve its compatibility with other tools available on the Steering Group’s website. For further information on the questionnaire, please refer to the relevant webpage. The HKMA itself adheres to the latest global standards by providing high-quality sustainable disclosures in its “Sustainability Report,” thereby demonstrating its own commitment to sustainability. The report contains detailed information on climate-related operational risks faced by the HKMA, as well as its plans and progress toward achieving climate-related objectives. For specifics on the HKMA’s own sustainability disclosures, please refer to the “HKMA and Sustainability” section. Given the rapidly evolving nature of the sustainable finance landscape, the HKMA is intensifying efforts to build skills within the banking sector and promote knowledge sharing with other regulators and international stakeholders, aiming to bridge existing knowledge and talent gaps. To enhance local bankers’ understanding and capabilities in sustainable finance, the HKMA, in collaboration with the Hong Kong Institute of Bankers, launched the foundational level of the “Green and Sustainable Finance” module under the “Banking Professional Qualifications Framework” in July 2023. This module aims to help banking professionals acquire relevant knowledge and develop competencies in green and sustainable finance more effectively, covering four main areas: (1) green and sustainable financial products and services; (2) sustainable/climate risk management; (3) sustainable disclosure and reporting; and (4) sustainable strategies, compliance, and governance. Additionally, the professional level of the “Green and Sustainable Finance” module, targeted at mid- to senior-level bankers, was launched in November. To provide necessary training for banking professionals, the Hong Kong Institute of Bankers, as the administrator of the “Green and Sustainable Finance” module, introduced foundational-level training courses in May. Following the launch of the professional level in November, the HKMA will collaborate with the banking sector in 2025 to develop a professional-level training course. To better understand the banking industry’s evolving skill and training needs, the HKMA is currently partnering with industry stakeholders on a study titled “Future Banking Talent 2026–2030,” with findings scheduled for release in 2025. This joint research effort serves as a follow-up to the “Future Banking Talent 2021–2025” report published in June 2020. The outcomes of this follow-up study will provide valuable guidance for the industry in formulating and adjusting talent development strategies and measures, thereby supporting the sustainable growth of the banking sector. Through collaboration with the Steering Group, the HKMA also continues to facilitate the implementation of the government-funded “Pilot Scheme on Green and Sustainable Finance Training,” which subsidizes training related to sustainable finance for industry practitioners, graduates, and students. As of December 2024, a total of 85 international and local courses have been registered as eligible training programs under this scheme, with over 5,700 reimbursement applications approved. In its “Budget 2025–26,” the government announced that this scheme will be extended through 2028. Leveraging its expertise, the HKMA actively promotes skills development and knowledge exchange through regional and international cooperation. As a founding member of the Capacity Building for Sustainable Investment Alliance (CASI), the HKMA’s Infrastructure Financing Facilitation Office co-hosted a two-day training workshop in Hong Kong in June, focusing on global sustainable finance markets, policy frameworks, and innovative financial tools. Furthermore, the HKMA supported the establishment of a Hong Kong chapter of the Glasgow Financial Alliance for Net Zero (GFANZ) in October, and will utilize GFANZ’s network and expertise to further strengthen skills development in transition planning and transition finance.

As a major global asset owner and manager, the HKMA actively leads the development of green and sustainable finance. Leveraging its experience in demonstrating that financial performance and positive impact can go hand in hand, the HKMA adheres to responsible investment principles in managing the Exchange Fund. It gives priority to sustainable assets and requires its external investment managers to actively exercise their rights as asset owners. Guided by the principle of “preserving capital while seeking long-term appreciation,” the HKMA invests prudently, believing that due consideration of environmental, social and governance (ESG) factors helps mitigate investment risks while unlocking long-term sustainable value. As a committed signatory to the Principles for Responsible Investment (PRI), the HKMA is dedicated to advancing its responsible investment efforts. We place special emphasis on sustainability, particularly the pressing issue of climate change, with the aim of enhancing the resilience of the Exchange Fund and achieving better risk-adjusted long-term returns. We incorporate ESG factors in a pragmatic and orderly manner, continuously exploring various investment tools to channel capital into sustainable investments across different asset classes (Figure 1). Through its role as a major investor, the HKMA contributes to the growth of the green and sustainable finance ecosystem. In September, it released the “HKMA ESG Expectations” and made the document available to its investment partners via its annual ESG workshop and website. We collaborate with like-minded investors, regulators and international organisations to develop industry standards and promote the adoption of responsible investment practices within the financial sector and central banking community. Through these joint efforts, we strive to foster a future where finance and sustainable development progress hand in hand. In October, the HKMA unveiled its “Sustainable Finance Action Plan” (the “Action Plan”), which further reinforces its commitment to investing in a sustainable future by aiming to achieve net-zero emissions by 2050 through the Exchange Fund’s portfolio and by mobilising partners to support the transition to a low-carbon economy. The Exchange Fund Advisory Committee, chaired by the Financial Secretary, sets out the responsible investment framework and guiding principles, which are implemented by the Exchange Fund Investment Office in the management of the Fund’s investments. The primary guiding principle establishes the overall tone for the HKMA to balance responsible investment practices with the Exchange Fund’s investment objectives. The Investment Committee under the Advisory Committee, chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, oversees ESG and climate-related risks associated with the Exchange Fund’s investments. It reviews the responsible investment framework and risk management policies, and monitors their implementation through regular reports submitted by the Sustainable Investment Team of the Exchange Fund Investment Office. As shown in Figure 2, the ESG Committee under the Exchange Fund Investment Office, chaired by the Chief Strategy Officer, coordinates and oversees all ESG-related activities within the Office. Proposals and progress updates discussed at its quarterly meetings are reported to the Chief Executive of the Exchange Fund Investment Office. Additionally, the Green and Sustainable Steering Committee, chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA and comprising the Chief Executive and Chief Strategy Officer of the Exchange Fund Investment Office, meets regularly to provide guidance on ESG policies and measures across various HKMA functions, including the Exchange Fund Investment Office, so as to achieve the HKMA’s overall ESG objectives. The Sustainable Investment Group collaborates closely with various teams within the Exchange Fund Investment Office in integrating ESG factors into investment practices. It also assists senior management at the Exchange Fund Investment Office in managing ESG-related risks and opportunities—particularly those related to climate—across all types of investments:  – Public market investments: The Credit, Regulatory and Oversight Committee, composed of senior officials from the Exchange Fund Investment Office, reviews how ESG factors are incorporated into credit risk models based on input from the Sustainable Investment Group. Meanwhile, the Risk Management and Oversight Department regularly monitors the ESG performance of the fixed-income portfolio. Additionally, the Sustainable Investment Group participates from an ESG perspective in the selection, appointment, and oversight of external fund managers managing the equity portfolio (for details, please refer to the section “Promoting Active Ownership” under “Risk Management” on page 39).  – Private market investments: The Investment Committee, chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, considers ESG-related assessments provided by both the private market investment and risk management teams for each proposed investment. The HKMA recognises that physical and transition risks associated with climate change, as well as related opportunities, can affect the long-term financial performance of Exchange Fund investments. According to the United Nations Environment Programme’s “Emissions Gap Report 2024”, unless there is a global, large-scale effort to rapidly cut greenhouse gas emissions, the global average temperature is expected to rise by 2.6 to 3.1 degrees Celsius above pre-industrial levels. Uncertainties surrounding policy changes, technological developments, and shifts in behaviour in response to rising temperatures may exacerbate transition risks, leading to heightened market volatility and impacting asset valuations. At the same time, the increasing frequency and severity of extreme weather events pose additional risks of physical damage and financial losses to investments. Amid these challenges, governments and industries worldwide are turning to sustainable solutions, thereby creating potentially attractive long-term investment opportunities in low-carbon technologies, emerging innovations, and sustainable infrastructure. The HKMA believes that investing in a sustainable future aligns with the Exchange Fund’s investment objectives; hence, it places special emphasis on climate-related considerations when integrating ESG factors. The HKMA has set a target for the Exchange Fund portfolio to achieve net-zero emissions by 2050, and it is pursuing this goal through a structured three-pronged approach (see Diagram 3). In 2024, the HKMA released an “Action Plan” that further solidifies its commitments and efforts related to climate transition (see Diagram 4). To support the transition to a low-carbon economy, the HKMA favours proactive engagement rather than outright exclusion or divestment from investable assets.  Investing in a sustainable future: – The Exchange Fund portfolio aims to achieve net-zero emissions by 2050. – Actively expand the scope and variety of sustainable investments, especially those focused on climate transition in both public and private markets. – Integrate ESG factors—with particular attention to climate change and transition prospects—into every investment decision. – Establish clear ESG expectations that conform to international standards and best practices, and require all external fund managers, investee companies, and counterparties to adhere to them. – Strive to reduce the weighted average carbon intensity (WACI) of the Exchange Fund’s equity portfolio by 67% from its 2017 level by 2030.  Supporting regional transition through investment: – Continue engaging with external fund managers to optimise investment opportunities that drive transition efforts. – Keep identifying and prioritising high-quality investment opportunities that facilitate Asia’s transition while delivering positive global impacts.  First and foremost, maintaining a diversified and robust portfolio is essential to fulfilling the Exchange Fund’s primary investment objectives. Excluding certain sectors or industries outright would narrow the pool of investable assets, potentially affecting both investment returns and risk profiles. Through a compatible approach, the HKMA can seize opportunities to invest in enterprises undergoing transformation—including those in high-emission industries—that possess advanced technologies and sound corporate governance to adapt to evolving global climate trends. Secondly, addressing climate change necessitates the transformation of core “brown” industries. Merely excluding or divesting from relevant investments will not help resolve carbon emissions issues. Instead, by deploying strategic capital and actively exercising its asset ownership rights, the HKMA supports these industries in transitioning toward sustainable and low-carbon practices, thereby bringing about beneficial changes both for itself and globally. The HKMA’s net-zero investment policy has evolved from a preference for green or low-carbon assets to also encompassing assets with credible transition prospects, thereby driving overall economy-wide decarbonisation. As a global asset owner, the HKMA recognises that the long-term resilience of its portfolio depends not only on portfolio adjustments but also on broader economic transformation. Although there is no single perfect solution, in 2024 the HKMA refined its responsible investment strategy by adopting a comprehensive and diversified approach to foster such transformation while supporting both the Exchange Fund and global net-zero objectives. This strategy integrates top-down and bottom-up tools, including the incorporation of ESG factors and stewardship into fundamental analysis, portfolio decarbonisation tilts, and thematic investments targeting various asset classes aligned with pathways toward net-zero emissions. In public markets, this may involve tilting the portfolio toward ESG leaders or firms offering climate solutions, coupled with stewardship efforts to drive corporate transformation. In private markets, greater emphasis is placed on investments that facilitate such transition. By integrating ESG factors into investment decisions, the HKMA continues to identify opportunities that promote climate transition while enhancing the long-term resilience of the Exchange Fund’s portfolio. Sustainable investments across different asset classes now account for over 10% of the Exchange Fund’s overall portfolio, with financial performance comparable to relevant portfolio benchmarks (Figure 5).  – Public market investments: The HKMA has launched an active global equity portfolio focused on sustainability and climate transition, and extended the application of customised low-carbon equity indices to two additional portfolios managed by external investment managers. The HKMA also continues to seek green, social and sustainability (GSS) bonds that offer competitive returns while financing sustainable projects (see the section “Enhancing Sustainability through GSS Bonds” for relevant case studies).  – Private market investments: The HKMA strives to build a robust long-term growth portfolio by capitalising on investment opportunities aligned with climate and energy transition themes. Leveraging its extensive network and expertise, it actively identifies and evaluates investments capable of accelerating energy transition, including through strategic partnerships with multinational organisations (see the section “Collaborating to Address Climate Challenges in Asia and Beyond” for examples). Passive investment portfolios that use ESG indices as investment benchmarks; customized decarbonization strategies applied to passive and active quantitative investment portfolios whose benchmarks are non-ESG indices; active investment portfolios focused on governance; active ESG investment portfolios centered on sustainability and climate transition; sustainable projects such as renewable energy infrastructure, as well as green-certified buildings and warehouses; funds dedicated to energy transition and decarbonization efforts worldwide, in Asia, and in the Global South; green, social responsibility, and sustainability bonds; a green bond fund managed by an international organization; the “Managed Co-Lending Portfolio Program” (MCPP) administered by the International Finance Corporation, which focuses on financing sustainable projects in emerging markets; and the “MCPP One Planet” initiative, which offers climate-related investments in emerging markets aligned with the Paris Agreement.  The Monetary Authority of Macao invested in green bonds issued by a quasi-governmental entity. The funds raised through these green bonds were allocated to multiple projects, including upgrading outdated equipment at various wastewater treatment facilities. These upgrades involved optimizing monitoring and control systems as well as pump performance, thereby generating positive environmental benefits in wastewater management, waste reduction, and recycling processes. In addition to continuously treating wastewater and sludge, these facilities compost or repurpose dewatered sludge to produce fertilizers, charcoal, cement, and other construction materials, achieving a sludge recycling rate of up to 100%. They also utilize gases generated during sludge treatment to power boilers and generate electricity.  The Monetary Authority of Macao also invested in green bonds issued by a multilateral development bank. These bonds financed numerous projects, including the restoration of a national canal system. As one of the country’s largest irrigation systems, these canals are designed to channel excess river water to arid regions. The primary objective of this project is to repair deteriorating canal linings, thereby preventing leaks, conserving water, improving water-use efficiency, and reclaiming waterlogged land. Additionally, the project provides skill training for local stakeholders, promoting the adoption and effective use of modern irrigation techniques such as micro-irrigation, as well as sustainable farming practices.

The HKMA is committed to being a responsible and sustainable organization. In 2024, one of its key priorities in fulfilling this commitment is to advance its target date for achieving net-zero emissions in its operations to 2030—20 years earlier than originally planned—in line with the Sustainable Finance Action Plan. Apart from promoting environmental sustainability, the HKMA also pledges to foster staff training, physical and mental well-being, financial inclusion, and public financial literacy. The Green and Sustainable Development Steering Committee, chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, serves as the main decision-making body for all organizational sustainability initiatives. Demonstrating its commitment to addressing climate change, the Steering Committee approved in October 2024 a new target for the HKMA to achieve net-zero emissions in its operations by 2030, as part of the Sustainable Finance Action Plan. At the departmental level, the Assistant Chief Executive (Institutional Development and Operations) provides guidance on implementing sustainability measures related to operations, staff well-being, and social engagement, and regularly reports to the Steering Committee. The Administration Division acts as the coordinator and central hub for executing, communicating, and reporting on these sustainability efforts. Complementary support is also provided by the Green Office Task Force and the Volunteer Service Group, both composed of staff from various operational departments; the former serves as a platform for brainstorming ideas on creating a greener workplace, while the latter aims to cultivate a culture of volunteerism among staff. In recognition of the HKMA’s dedication to environmental protection, staff welfare, and broader societal responsibility, the Hong Kong Council of Social Service has awarded the HKMA the “15 Years+ Caring Partnership” badge for 18 consecutive years from 2006 to 2024. The HKMA’s sustainability strategy continues to be structured around three pillars: environmental stewardship, staff welfare, and social responsibility.   - Focus on carbon reduction and digitalization in daily operations, with the goal of achieving net-zero emissions by 2030.   - Adopt green procurement requirements in accordance with government guidelines.   - Promote more environmentally friendly practices within the financial sector and society at large.   - Build a motivated workforce and talent pool to meet the HKMA’s strategic objectives.   - Foster a collaborative, inclusive, and caring workplace that values diversity and strengthens staff belongingness.   - Provide a high-quality working environment that encourages healthy lifestyles.   - Cultivate a culture of social awareness.   - Integrate social considerations into procurement processes and supply chain management.   - Promote financial inclusion and enhance public financial literacy through consumer education initiatives.    The HKMA takes climate change seriously and leads by example. In October 2024, it announced plans to advance its target date for net-zero emissions in its operations to 2030—20 years earlier than previously committed—as part of the Action Plan. The HKMA has revised its roadmap toward net-zero transition, emphasizing responsible management of its environmental impact through carbon reduction, energy conservation, paper minimization, waste recycling, and leveraging improvements in the local power utility’s fuel mix. Additionally, it has transitioned to a digital work environment to boost efficiency while lowering its carbon footprint. Recognizing the importance of nurturing a sustainability-oriented culture, the HKMA continuously runs promotional programs and activities to encourage staff to adopt environmentally responsible practices. Under its primary 2030 net-zero target, the HKMA is exploring the use of carbon-embedded tools across its value chain to further cut emissions and is committed to low-carbon procurement wherever possible. Since 2023, it has fully offset carbon emissions from business travel by purchasing sustainable aviation fuel and participating in carbon offset programs. The HKMA intends to extend these carbon-embedding and offset initiatives to cover all other major sources of emissions. Beyond these operational commitments, the HKMA continues to drive market-wide low-carbon transition efforts, ranging from implementing electronic document submission and processing systems to promoting electronic payments and facilitating the return of coins into circulation. The remainder of this chapter elaborates on the HKMA’s strategies for environmental leadership, staff well-being, and social responsibility. Within the HKMA’s overall enterprise risk management framework, the Risk Committee chaired by the Chief Executive oversees and reviews potential risks and threats—including those arising from climate change—that the HKMA may face in its daily operations. To more effectively assess how climate change might impact its operations, the HKMA has identified various climate-related risks and examined both their actual and potential effects. To mitigate these risks while ensuring uninterrupted operations, the HKMA has incorporated multiple measures into its office operations aimed at reducing potential physical hazards, fire risks, and other emergencies. Additionally, the HKMA regularly updates its contingency plans to include comprehensive measures covering not only its offices but also its communications and IT infrastructure. Periodic evacuation drills and exercises involving backup facilities are conducted to ensure staff remain prepared to implement these contingency measures. The HKMA also continuously monitors its transition risks by tracking greenhouse gas emissions, waste generation, energy consumption, and paper usage stemming from its own operations. Its latest climate target is to achieve net-zero greenhouse gas emissions across Scope 1, Scope 2, and Scope 3 related to its operations by 2030 at the latest. These targets were established following the methodology outlined by the Science Based Targets initiative. The HKMA utilizes the Greenhouse Gas Protocol to measure and report its emissions. Scope 1 emissions refer to direct emissions from petrol-powered vehicles. Given the nature of its operations, the majority of the HKMA’s greenhouse gas emissions fall under Scope 2—indirect emissions resulting from electricity generated by burning fossil fuels. In the absence of supplier-specific data, the HKMA employs a conservative approach to estimate major Scope 3 emissions arising from purchased goods, including capital equipment, and services. Other relevant Scope 3 emissions include waste sent to landfills as well as air travel and commuting by staff. Detailed calculations for 2023 and 2024 are presented in the “Performance Summary” on page 50. The performance data disclosed by the HKMA has been independently verified by the Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency; the scope and baseline of this verification are detailed in the “Verification Statement” appended at the end of this report. The HKMA practices what it preaches, adhering to the same climate-related standards it expects banks under its supervision and the broader financial sector to follow. As a first step toward greener mobility, the HKMA began replacing its petrol-powered vehicles with electric ones in 2024, with plans to continue this transition throughout 2025 to achieve fully eco-friendly transportation. Environmental considerations remain integral to the design, operation, and maintenance of the HKMA’s offices. Specifically, during various renovation projects in 2024, the HKMA prioritized reusing existing furniture and interior materials or offering trade-in discounts on new items to minimize waste generation. To further enhance overall energy efficiency, the HKMA regularly reviews energy consumption patterns and conservation measures across its offices and data centers. In 2024, it incorporated a modular design for its uninterruptible power supply systems during data center upgrades, thereby further improving the Power Usage Effectiveness (PUE) rating of its Green Building Council-certified data centers. This design allows for flexible capacity expansion, improved operational efficiency under partial load conditions, and integration of advanced cooling technologies and higher power density—all contributing to reduced overall energy consumption. Through its digital workplace initiatives, the HKMA has strengthened virtual collaboration while streamlining workflows, effectively curbing paper usage. Additionally, by aligning with manufacturers’ software update cycles, the HKMA extends the usable lifespan of its mobile and desktop devices, thereby prolonging their safe operational period. To minimize office waste, the HKMA adheres to the “4R” principles—refuse, reduce, reuse, and recycle—and conducts regular waste audits to formulate targeted waste management strategies. Recycling bins for various materials are strategically placed throughout the office premises. To further boost recycling rates, the HKMA introduced dedicated bins for beverage cartons and plastic produce bags in 2024. Since November 2022, food waste collected at the office has been sent to a local waste-to-energy facility. In May 2024, the HKMA joined the Environmental Protection Department’s “Waste Reduction Commitment” initiative, pledging to implement measures aimed at curbing waste generation across all organizational activities. The HKMA continues to prioritize procurement of goods meeting the environmental specifications outlined in the Government’s “Green Procurement List,” particularly electrical appliances and office consumables. To reduce carbon emissions from air travel, staff are encouraged to plan their trips meticulously—for instance, by consolidating multiple overseas trips into a single itinerary whenever feasible. At the institutional level, the HKMA has been purchasing sustainable aviation fuel since 2023, thereby reducing annual carbon emissions from air travel by approximately 10%. Furthermore, the HKMA participates in the Gold Standard certified carbon offset program to offset any remaining emissions from air travel; this program focuses on renewable energy generation and electrification projects in emerging markets. In 2024, the HKMA organized numerous learning activities for its staff, such as lectures and guided tours of waste-to-energy facilities, to deepen their understanding of environmental sustainability issues. Starting from Earth Day on April 22, 2024, and throughout the entire month of May, the HKMA held its inaugural “HKMA Green Month” under the theme “Green Thinking, Green Living, Green Working.” This served as an excellent opportunity for the HKMA to demonstrate its commitment and drive toward integrating environmental sustainability into its internal operations. Activities included a “Sustainability BINGO Scorecard” designed to encourage staff to adopt greener lifestyles, a “Save the Earth” quiz, and a workshop on caring for indoor plants using “kokedama” techniques originating from Japan. Additionally, the results of a waste audit were shared, and representatives from a local recycling center provided insights into best practices in recycling. To sustain the momentum generated by the Green Month, the HKMA launched a six-month recycling campaign in October, emphasizing responsible waste management and underscoring how even minor individual behavioral changes can significantly enhance the organization’s overall recycling performance. A highlight of this campaign was the release of a video series titled “Green ‘Fit’ Actions,” in which senior executives offered practical recycling tips. The campaign also featured a range of screen savers, eye-catching posters, intranet articles, and electronic reminders aimed at motivating staff to reduce waste and increase recycling efforts. At the end of 2024, the HKMA conducted an employee survey to gauge their awareness of sustainability issues and to gather feedback on proposed green office initiatives. The findings will inform the development of future sustainability training programs and waste management strategies. As Hong Kong’s central banking authority, the HKMA regards itself as a key agent of change; consequently, it strives to accelerate the low-carbon transition by promoting sustainable practices within the financial sector and broader society. The HKMA has implemented multiple measures to enhance the efficiency of its external processes. Following the successful launch of the “Common Data Submission Platform” in 2023, the HKMA expanded its services in 2024 to include non-bank entities such as operators of stored-value payment instruments, thereby facilitating their submission of certain regulatory data. This expansion aims to further streamline reporting procedures for all participating entities, providing a smoother user experience while reinforcing the HKMA’s dedication to sustainability. Other new initiatives introduced in 2024 include SurveyTool, which enables banks to respond to HKMA questionnaires via a simplified submission process, and an intelligent information and document management system that offers users a centralized platform featuring advanced search capabilities tailored to banking-related documents.

The Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency conducted an independent verification of the environmental data (“Data”) of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (“HKMA”). The Data includes total energy consumption in 2024, Scope 1 and Scope 2 greenhouse gas emissions, paper usage, non-hazardous waste generated (including general waste and recyclable waste sent to landfills), greenhouse gas emissions from air travel, as well as their respective intensity values. Additionally, the Data covers Scope 3 greenhouse gas emissions arising from purchases of goods and services, capital goods, fuel and energy-related activities, non-hazardous waste (including general waste and recyclable waste sent to landfills), and employee commuting in both 2023 and 2024, together with their corresponding intensity values. The HKMA’s greenhouse gas emission data was compiled in accordance with the Greenhouse Gas Protocol (“GHG Protocol”) jointly issued by the World Resources Institute and the World Business Council for Sustainable Development. The verification covered a total of six office and warehouse assets: five offices located at 1) Two International Finance Centre, 2) Hopewell Centre, 3) One Pacific Place, 4) Kowloon Trade Centre, and 5) International Commerce Centre; the warehouse is situated at 6) Lok Sing Industrial Centre in Kwai Chung. The purpose of the verification was to provide reasonable assurance regarding the accuracy and reliability of the Data, as well as to confirm the adequacy of the HKMA’s data collection mechanisms. Within the scope of verification, the Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency examined representative samples of data and supporting evidence from 6 assets. This verification was carried out in compliance with the “International Standard on Assurance Engagements 3000 (Revised)” issued by the International Auditing and Assurance Standards Board, specifically the provisions pertaining to “Assurance Engagements Other Than Audits or Reviews of Historical Financial Information.” The verification procedures were designed to enable the formation of an opinion and to provide a reasonable level of assurance. These procedures adhered to the requirements set forth in the GHG Protocol. To assess data integrity and accuracy, the verification process entailed tracing selected sample data back to their sources; it also involved reviewing the basic procedures for data collection, aggregation, estimation, calculation, and internal checks, followed by reliability testing. Furthermore, the internal data collection and management mechanisms were evaluated through interviews with personnel responsible for data preparation, and representative data and documentation were examined. All relevant raw data and supporting evidence were thoroughly reviewed during the verification process. The HKMA bears responsibility for data collection and reporting. Our verification work was conducted in complete independence and impartiality; the verification team at the Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency had no involvement whatsoever in the data preparation process. Based on the results of this verification, the Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency can reasonably assure that:   – The Data is substantially accurate and reliable;   – The HKMA’s overall data collection mechanisms are adequate.
